(01)Case Study · Agriculture Commerce

Bajoma.

Commerce infrastructure connecting smallholder farmers to urban buyers across Cameroon — designed for the realities of low bandwidth, informal trust, and last-mile distribution.

RoleLead Product Designer
Timeline2 Months · 2025
ContextRural Commerce, CM
FocusTrust + Offline UX
PlatformWeb · Mobile
"Many farmers relied on unstable mobile connections. We reduced page weight by 70% and recovered 3x more completed orders."Outcome · Field Validation

Trust before transaction.

Smallholder farmers were already selling — through brokers, cooperatives, and word of mouth. The product had to feel safer than the system it replaced, not flashier.

The early prototype had every modern e-commerce convention. Adoption stalled. Field interviews surfaced the same sentence, repeatedly: "How do I know my money moved?"

Receipts had to survive offline.
Order status had to be readable in sunlight.
Cancellation had to feel reversible, not punitive.
Payment confirmation needed a human-readable signal.
(01.2)System Decisions

Interface decisions that moved the metric.

01Decisions

Offline-first receipts

Every transaction generates a printable receipt token cached locally. The interface treats connectivity as optional, not assumed.

02Decisions

Trust column over star ratings

Replaced 5-star reviews with verified-delivery counts. Numbers a farmer could trust over opinions they couldn't trace.

03Decisions

USSD bridge as a first-class flow

Critical actions — status check, dispute, payout — work over USSD. The app is the polish layer, not the gatekeeper.

04Decisions

Two-tap commit

Order placement collapsed from 7 taps to 2. The lost interactions weren't decisions — they were friction.

05Decisions

Sunlight-mode UI

High-contrast palette for outdoor readability. Tested in market stalls, not just in studio.

06Decisions

Green as the trust signal

Reserved a single accent for actions that affect money. Consistency taught the eye where to look.

Bajoma is the case study most reflective of how I think. The other systems extend the same posture into different markets.

(02)Case Study · Selected Systems

Projina.

A centralized operations platform connecting field teams to back-office workflows — designed for productivity, visibility, and efficient internal management across distributed businesses.

RoleLead Product Designer
Timeline5 Months · 2025–2026
ContextRural Commerce, CM
FocusTrust + Offline UX
PlatformWeb · Mobile
"Operational visibility doesn't come from more data, but from the right data surfaced at the right time and hierarchy."Design Principle

Operations break where systems don't connect.

Most growing businesses run on a patchwork — spreadsheets, messaging apps, paper forms, and a few disconnected tools. As teams scale, visibility collapses. Decisions get made on missing information.

Projina had to feel powerful without becoming overwhelming — an operations system, not an operations dashboard.

Tools disconnected across teams and locations.
Employee activity invisible without manual reporting.
Task status scattered across multiple surfaces.
Reporting workflows slow and reactive, not proactive.
Preview live
(02.2)System Decisions

Operational decisions that compressed daily friction.

01Decisions

Single operational surface

Tasks, teams, and reports unified into one navigation model. No more cross-tool reconciliation.

02Decisions

Status as primary signal

Every record exposes its operational state first. Detail is a click, status is a glance.

03Decisions

Field-to-office continuity

Mobile field updates flow directly into back-office reporting. No manual data re-entry.

04Decisions

Density tuned per role

Field workers see a card; managers see a table; leadership sees a chart. Same record, three surfaces.

05Decisions

Reporting in two clicks

Operational reports collapse into pre-built views. Custom is available; default is fast.

06Decisions

Sunlight-mode field forms

High-contrast, large-tap-target forms designed for outdoor environments on older Android phones.

Projina is a study in operational restraint — proof that scaling a business doesn't require scaling its complexity.

(03)Case Study · Brand Conversion

Crestlancing.

A modern web experience focused on trust, communication, and conversion — designed to strengthen credibility and translate brand presence into measurable engagement.

RoleDesigner
Timeline2 Weeks · 2026
ContextEmerging Brand
FocusClarity + Trust
PlatformWeb
"Outdated interfaces reduced productivity. We introduced a modern design system that accelerated workflows and improved platform adoption."Outcome · Field Validation

Clarity builds confidence. Confidence converts.

The previous experience lacked structure: unclear messaging, outdated visuals, and a layout that buried the company's actual value. Visitors arrived without context and left without action.

The brief was simple, the constraint was severe — improve credibility, communicate clearly, and convert without inflating the experience.

Hero messaging didn't communicate the offer.
Visual hierarchy buried the most important content.
Trust signals were absent or generic.
Conversion paths were unclear across screen sizes.
(03.2)System Decisions

UI decisions for a confident, conversion-focused brand.

01Decisions

Single-line hero promise

Replaced paragraph hero copy with a single line stating the outcome. Bounce rate dropped immediately.

02Decisions

Services framed as outcomes

Service cards lead with the user's result, not the company's process. Engagement followed.

03Decisions

Architectural typography

Strong type hierarchy carried the brand. Decoration was kept off the page.

04Decisions

Conversion-focused layout system

Every section ends with a CTA tuned to its intent — never a generic "contact us."

05Decisions

Responsive-first structure

Designed mobile-up. The desktop version is the mobile version with breathing room — not a different page.

06Decisions

Performance budget as brand value

Sub-280KB page weight became part of the brand promise: fast loads as a credibility signal.

Crestlancing is a study in restraint — proof that a brand's most modern asset is often the clarity it refuses to compromise.
